newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast gasoline prices fall on trader talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast gasoline prices fall on trader talk.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast gasoline fell early Wednesday, lowered by traders who wanted to drum up sales after several days of lackluster trade, players said.

Bearish traders claimed four to five cargoes of product, due later this month, would replenish inventories, which last week stood 2.3 million barrels below year-ago, American Petroleum Institute (API) said in its Tuesday stocks report.
"It's getting beat up, but there's no reason," one trader said. "Things are fundamentally well-balanced."

Gasoline stocks on hand at West Coast (PADD IV) refineries rose 323,000 barrels to 26.9 million last week, API said. But despite the year-on-year shortfall, traders said, production was steady rebounding after seasonal maintenance shutdowns.
West Coast refineries operated at 91 percent of capacity last week, up 1.2 percentage points from the previous week, API reported Tuesday.
Offers for CARB gasoline in Los Angeles were talked 70.50, 2.50 cents a gallon lower in early Wednesday trade. San Francisco CARB gasoline was priced two cents lower by sellers at 69.50 cents.
CARB diesel fuel rose one cent in Los Angeles to 76/77 cents a gallon, following heating oil futures prices in New York, which rose 0.21 cents a gallon by 1207 PDT.
